implementation_notes.global_ux_causality: The global ux causality block ablates pre-probe ux by resetting all layers to the static baseline u=U and x=1 before probe. In Figure 4, the left panel tests whether globally ablating ux reduces L3 bias magnitude, and the right panel compares intact dynamic, ux-ablated, and full_static final decision-vector magnitudes to assess whether ux ablation drives the system toward static behavior.
implementation_notes.layer_mask_mapping: layer1 uses input-resolution probe partitions; layer2 applies boolean max-pooling with net.pool1; layer3 uses the real layer2 receptive-field support followed by boolean max-pooling with net.pool2.
implementation_notes.main_outputs: Main saved outputs emphasize abs(DPI_L3), final decision-vector magnitude, their matched-region per-area normalizations, matched-region ux, matched-region ux mass, and the reduction in Block D effect strength after global ux ablation.
implementation_notes.matched_region_rule: Per-area and ux analyses for only_SP, only_DP, and only_SDP use only the corresponding matched probe region and do not aggregate unmatched regions.
implementation_notes.supplementary_union_reweighting: A supplementary union-vs-complement ux reweighting experiment tests whether probe-evoked L3 input dynamics are reshaped because overlap-relevant regions carry elevated pre-probe ux. The union region is defined as SP union DP union SDP, and the complement region is the remaining probe foreground. Region-selective ux ablation on the union region should reduce union contribution to the L3 input map more strongly than ablation on the complement region.
implementation_notes.ux_visualization: Current ux figures use L1/L2/L3-averaged summary values for trend-focused visualization. The goal is to preserve region-level trends rather than compare layer-specific differences.

main_conclusions.region_effect: SP, DP, and SDP differ in unit-area effect strength, as quantified by abs(DPI_L3) / area and ||delta_v|| / area under the matched-region-only conditions.
main_conclusions.region_ux: The ux visualization now uses a trend-focused L1/L2/L3 average. The three-layer-averaged matched-region ux follows the same SP / DP / SDP trend as the region effect analysis, and matched-region ux mass predicts effect strength.
main_conclusions.ux_causality: Global ux ablation reduces both |DPI_L3| and ||delta_v||. The overlap_union region carries higher ux than the complement, and union-region ux ablation weakens both L3 input contribution weights and downstream response strength.

mechanistic_quantity_of_interest: raw pre-probe STSP ux = u * x

region_definitions.DP: distractor intersect probe and not sample
region_definitions.SP: sample intersect probe and not distractor

scientific_hypothesis: SP, DP, and SDP differ in per-area effect strength on L3 bias magnitude and final decision-vector magnitude. Those per-area differences correspond to matched-region pre-probe ux, and matched-region ux mass predicts raw effect strength. A global pre-probe ux ablation causally tests whether L3 bias magnitude and final decision-vector magnitude remain when dynamic ux is removed before probe.

supplementary_union_reweight_regions.complement: probe foreground not covered by the overlap_union region
